detail: Packet-vocabulary disposition: structural_zero_treat_as_missing for the McBee town polygon, with the repair path being a footprint/attribution check rather than a value fill. The agency has NEVER recorded a positive Part-I year in 2018-2024, and five of those seven years contain no submission of any kind (SRS 0 months and no NIBRS row at all in 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2023). Even at half the peer rate (2/yr) seven straight zeros is ~8e-7. To make this record likely you need a true rate below roughly 0.3 offences a year — under 40 per 100k, sustained, for a town that maintains its own police department. That is not a reachable crime outcome; it is a description of a filing practice. EST2024 = 0 [observedx7] is NOT defensible as a measured zero. That is a crosswalk-attribution defect, not something a peer fill should paper over. Verify against the Chesterfield County Sheriff ORI's series and footprint before filling; if the sheriff-attribution story does not hold, a peer fill for the band is the fallback.

Composition is unscoreable (no positive full year anywhere in the span), so the level test carries the ruling, and the level test is decisive at the seven-year horizon in a way it is not for any single year. I hold this at medium rather than high because two quite different mechanisms fit the same rows — a genuine near-zero-crime town whose few incidents are reported by the county, versus an ORI that files empty headers — and they imply different repairs (footprint reassignment versus imputation). The flag itself is safe under either; the repair is not, so I name it as an open question instead of choosing.

detail: Packet-vocabulary disposition: token_report_treat_as_partial — reject the 12-month NIBRS header for this agency-year. Believable months: at most 9 (the SRS record), and the count ratio implies far fewer. EST2024 = 8 [observedx7] is NOT defensible. FIRST DEFECT — the lane choice. The two lanes carry the identical count 8 but disagree on the denominator: NIB 8 at 12 months, SRS 8 at 9 months. The ladder selected NIB on reason 'greater_month_coverage', which for equal counts means it deliberately chose the LARGER denominator, maximising the implied completeness and denying the row any uplift. When two renderings of one submission agree on the count and differ on months, 'greater_month_coverage' is the wrong tiebreak — it should prefer the smaller measured months, or refuse the row. Minimum repair: annualise at 9 months, 8 x 12/9 = 10.7. SECOND DEFECT — the repair is still not credible. 2024's 8 offences is 12.3% of 2023's 65, and even the 9-month uplift reaches only 16%. At 3,808 population served that is 210 per 100k against 2023's 1,681 per 100k, for a county sheriff — sheriffs do not run at 210. The 12.3% ratio corresponds to roughly 1.5 months of the 2023 level, which is irreconcilable with a 9-month, let alone 12-month, submission. So: mark 2024 low-confidence/partial and, if a value is required, base it on the agency's own 2023 full year (65) rather than on the published 8 — while noting that 2023 is the ONLY real year in the record (2018-2022 are all 0 total on 0 reported months, i.e. five straight non-reports that should also be marked missing rather than zero, and the NIBRS lane first appears in 2023 despite a roster start of 2009-03-01), so a one-year baseline makes any fill shaky. THIRD, SEPARATE ITEM — footprint. This single county sheriff's counts are crosswalked at w=1 exclusive to '46:state_nonmunicipal_remainder (South Dakota nonmunicipal remainder)' by method 'auto_default'. That pools Fall River County's unincorporated crime into a statewide unincorporated bucket rather than Fall River County's own remainder. Worth confirming whether the statewide-remainder lane is the intended design for sheriffs or an auto_default fallback that is destroying county-level geography for SD's unincorporated areas; either way it is a distinct finding from the value ruling.
rationale: COMPOSITION OVER SLOPE is what decides this, and it cuts against the packet's own scorer. The scorer reports composition as NOT distorted because every stream with a baseline of 3+ retains 0-16% against a 12% aggregate — but that uniformity is the finding, not a clearance. Rape 1/2, agg assault 1/14, burglary 3/24, larceny 3/19, MVT 0/6: a preserved offence mix scaled down by ~88% in a single year is what fewer submitted records looks like, not what less crime looks like. Real crime declines do not move all seven streams by the same factor at once. Combined with a lane-months conflict (9 versus 12 on identical counts) and a ratio implying ~1.5 months of normal volume, the row cannot stand as a complete year. I hold medium rather than high because the counterfactual rests on a single baseline year from an agency that only began appearing in NIBRS in 2023, and because a genuine 88% drop from a staffing or contract-policing change (for instance a 2023 arrangement covering Hot Springs that ended in 2024) is not literally impossible — that alternative would be an ORI-footprint change rather than a reporting failure, and it would also make the published 8-as-complete wrong, so the flag holds either way while the repair value does not.

rationale: Seven consecutive complete (12-month) NIBRS years with never a single Part-I incident, for the only law-enforcement agency covering an entire county of ~1,400 people. This is precisely the named structural-non-reporting pattern: a never-positive multi-year history at pop >1,000. The peer-implied level is lambda 6.6/yr, which makes even ONE zero year a ~1-in-760 event and the seven-year run arithmetically unreachable; sustaining it would require a true county rate of ~35 per 100k, about a fourteenth of the band median, which is not a reachable crime outcome for 1,400 residents with exclusive county-wide coverage including all unincorporated territory. Every check that could rescue it is absent rather than favourable: no publication lane carries this ORI in any year (the CIUS ingest covers city/university/state-tribal tables, not county, so the absence is ingest coverage and carries no FBI quality signal either way), SRS is 0-months in all seven years so there is no independent lane, and composition is uniformly zero across all seven streams so it carries no signal. The 12-month header only establishes that twelve batches were filed, not that any records sat behind them - and an administratively perfect feed that has never once transmitted an incident is a non-report the pipeline read as data. Contrast Terrell County in this same batch: half the population and a third of the peer-implied rate, plus agency-supplied SRS-era zero returns and a proven non-filing year that shows its panel distinguishes filing from not filing. Carter has neither.

detail: Keep 2024 as observed at 7. Do not fill, and do not uplift the 7-month Return-A count. If anything is adjusted it is the screen, not the agency-year: the local_police 2.5-5k peer band is not an apt comparison for a residential township whose own baseline record was 83% larceny.

Coverage is not the story either way: the 7-of-12 Return-A months track the 7-offence total for a thin NIBRS filer, and a 7-month uplift would reach only 12 against a 27.5 baseline.

detail: Carry the published 2 (1 aggravated assault + 1 larceny) as observed. No uplift - the 12 months are genuinely submitted - and no fill. The lane check the packet asked for comes back clean: no larger equally complete submission was discarded.

detail: Do not carry 15 as a measured 12-month total. The record is internally inconsistent about its own coverage, and that is what the flag must say: the violent stream is consistent with a full year (8 aggravated assaults = 118 per 100k, ~98% of the peer-implied expectation of 8.2), while the property streams are consistent with barely one month (4 burglary + 3 larceny = 7 against the ~64 property offences the peer median implies for 6,761 residents, i.e. 11%). Separately, and independently of this ruling: the footprint is the Pennsylvania statewide overlap layer via fallback_overlap, which smears this department's mass across the whole state instead of its Armstrong County service area; that needs its own repair.
rationale: Composition, not slope, decides it. Larceny at 3 offences for 6,761 residents is 44 per 100k - roughly a tenth of the lowest credible municipal larceny floor and ~7% of the peer-implied larceny level - while aggravated assault sits at essentially its full expected level. Aggravated assault therefore accounts for 53% of this agency's 2024 Part-I total against a normal small-borough share of roughly 5-12%: an inverted composition, which is the signature of an untransmitted property stream rather than of a genuinely quiet jurisdiction. That reading is corroborated by provenance rather than resting on the peer gap alone: FBIpop is 0 through 2022 and 6,854 from 2023, so this is a newly stood-up regional department whose only prior filing is 2 offences on 8 months in 2023, and 2024 is its first full Return-A year; it is not a NIBRS reporter, SRS is the only lane present, and no CIUS or state publication exists to arbitrate. A brand-new department transmitting its violent stream in full and almost none of its property stream is a token record published as complete.

detail: 2024 must not stand as a tier-high, weight-1.0 observed zero. rationale: What separates Savoy from the other sub-1,000 zeros in this batch is that its own record establishes a materially positive rate which the hard zero contradicts. Henderson and Sebeka transmit ~0.2-0.26 offences/yr; Savoy transmitted 16 Part-I offences over 42 covered months (~4.6/yr, ABOVE its own band's peer-implied 3.9), including 5 in 2021 and 6 in 2022, before publishing an all-seven-stream zero. P(0) is ~1% against that pooled level and ~3% against a decay-weighted one; only against 2023 alone (1 offence on 7 months) does it become ordinary at ~18%, and a single seven-month draw is the weakest of the available rate estimates. Neither known-artefact test discriminates here - the 12-month header rules out blank-as-zero, the SRS 0-month figure is the back-conversion artefact this ORI shows in every zero-content year, and a uniform zero carries no composition signal - so the ruling rests on absolute plausibility against the agency's own demonstrated level, and there it fails. The asymmetry settles the direction: publishing this as observed x7 at tier high asserts, at the panel's highest confidence, that a 766-person town had no Part-I crime, on a 1-3% event and on a lane (CIUS) that is the same submission re-rendered; the alternative repair is ~2 offences drawn from the agency's own 2022-23 record, which is cheap and defensible. Confidence low because the header jump from 7 to 12 months in exactly the year content went to zero reads equally as compliance improvement (Texas's 2024 NIBRS push) and as a header-only automated feed, and nothing in the packet chooses.

detail: 2024 goes MISSING and fillable. But the three agreeing 2024 zeros are NOT corroboration: CIUS is the Return-A master frozen at publication and SRS/NIB are one submission rendered twice, so this is a single empty transmission — and with SRS at 0 filed months, that is the automatic-monthly-zero-report signature the packet names, not twelve measured months. COMPOSITION OVER SLOPE yields nothing either way (the zero is uniform across all streams, so the year carries no internal signal) — which removes the only evidence that could have supported a real collapse in level. UPLIFT CANNOT RESCUE A ZERO (0 x 12/n = 0), so token_reporting_flag would republish the identical zero; misread_missing is the only repair that changes the panel. OWN-HISTORY-LAUNDERING guarded by anchoring on 2022-2023 rather than the partial-year tail.

detail: Carry 44 as observed for 2024 (murder 0 / rape 3 / robbery 0 / agg assault 11 / burglary 3 / larceny 27 / MVT 0); no uplift, no fill. The peer-rate arm is the only screen that fired (277.4 vs 1327.2 per 100k, 20.9% of peers) and it is the one instrument that systematically misfires on this agency: 44 offences is the 2.5-month equivalent of a peer-normal 210/yr agency, which is the token signature by rate alone -- but the shape refuses it. A truncated 2.5-month slice of a peer-normal agency would be a proportionally scaled normal vector, with roughly 3-4 motor vehicle thefts and about one robbery surviving; instead MVT and robbery are exactly 0 while five streams are populated across both violent and property crime and larceny dominates at 27. That is the composition of a controlled-access, age-restricted population, not of a partial year -- and the roster's own name for the ORI, Hot Springs Village PD (a large gated retirement community; that characterization is outside-the-packet knowledge, flagged as such, but the roster name is panel evidence), is exactly the agency type the 10k-25k municipal peer band mis-specifies. The submission record is internally consistent: NIBRS start 2024-01-01 leaves at most 12 months inside coverage and the batch header is 12; there is no publication lane in any year, so there is no CIUS 12-month default and no blank-as-zero exposure; and no partial-year zero appears anywhere in the series. Medium rather than high because this is the ORI's only year on record with no cross-lane or publication corroboration, so first-year NIBRS under-filing cannot be positively excluded -- but nothing in the record indicates it, and the identity ruling (distinct_agencies vs AR0630100) already establishes the row is legitimately its own.

detail: 2024 goes MISSING and fillable; 2023 should be flagged MISSING on the same basis (0 filed months in SRS and no NIB row at all). ZERO believable months in 2024. OWN-HISTORY-LAUNDERING is the live trap: the degraded tail is 2022 (5 on 3-4 filed months) and 2023 (0 filed months), and anchoring there would put the base rate near 2.5 and make a live agency look defunct. COMPOSITION OVER SLOPE independently dates the record failure to 2022, well before the 2024 zero: 2022 composition is DISTORTED — burglary holds at 67% and agg assault at 60% of their own baselines while larceny falls to 5.9% and MVT to 0%, against an aggregate at 18%; larceny is 20% of that year's total versus 61% across baseline years. That spread is a change in WHICH streams are present, not in how much crime they describe, so 2022 is a degraded record, not a real low year, and cannot serve as a base rate. ABSOLUTE PLAUSIBILITY: at the baseline ~28/yr, P(true zero) ~7e-13; pop 966 is below the 1,500 floor so that arm does not fire, but even the peer rate (~6.8/yr) puts a true zero near 0.1%. UPLIFT CANNOT RESCUE A ZERO, so the year must go missing rather than be flagged partial.

detail: Carry 0 as observed for 2024, with two corrections that the ruling should not be applied without. (1) Provenance: re-point LANE_SELECTED_2024 from cius_publication_annual to nibrs_srs_equivalent_annual. The CIUS row is the frozen Return-A master sitting on 0 SRS filed months and has no independent standing; the NIB row (12 filed months) is the actual measurement and happens to carry the same value. Same number, correct source -- and the CIUS-over-NIB preference is precisely what produced the failures in the two PA cases in this batch. (2) Strike the 'NEVER-POSITIVE HISTORY / 7 consecutive all-lane zero years' signal from any support for this verdict: five of those seven years (2018-2022) have 0 filed months in every lane and carry no information in either direction. The entire basis is the 22 months of genuine NIBRS exposure in 2023 (10 filed months, total 0) and 2024 (12 filed months, total 0). No fill, no uplift.
rationale: The 2024 zero is backed by a real 12-month NIBRS submission, and for this ORI the NIB month field is demonstrably a measurement rather than a default: it moves, 10 in 2023 and 12 in 2024, tracking the roster NIBRS start of 2021-11-01. That excludes blank-as-zero (which requires a 0-2 month record) and yields two consecutive years of substantial filed exposure at zero. The two remaining false-zero mechanisms in the packet's own framing -- automatic monthly zero-reports after an agency stops producing records, and an ORI that keeps filing after policing moves to the sheriff -- both require a prior period of real record production that ended, and this ORI has none: no positive Part-I count in any lane in any year that had any exposure, so there is no transition to anchor either mechanism to. Population 828 sits below the 1,500 line where a crime-free year is unremarkable, peer expectation is only ~4.2 offences a year (503.4/100k), and the stake is mass_hint 0.0. Held at medium, not high: a 22-month zero against a ~4.2/yr peer expectation is ~4.5e-04 if the peer rate applied, which is uncomfortable -- though that peer median is a cross-type median and the smallest municipalities with a nominal PD run systematically under it. A Georgia GBI UCR agency table for Milner PD 2023-2024, or the department's staffing/dispatch record, would settle it; not escalated because the verdict question is answerable on this record.

detail: 2024 goes MISSING and fillable; do not carry observed 0x7. Fill at approximately 10 Part-I offences, anchored on the last demonstrably full-coverage span 2018-2021 (NIB 12-month years totalling 10, 7, 14, 9; mean 10.0, median 9.5), distributed on the baseline composition vector (larceny ~5.8, MVT ~2.5, burglary ~1.0, agg assault ~0.5, robbery ~0.2, murder 0, rape 0). The 2022 'collapse to 2' is an exposure artefact, not a decline: 2 offences on 2 Return-A filed months annualizes to ~12/yr, right at the 2018-2021 level, which removes the declining-trend story entirely. rationale: The 12-month NIBRS batch header cannot carry the completeness claim for this ORI, because for this ORI it is a constant, not a measurement: NIB reads 12 in every year 2018-2024, including 2023 and 2024 when Return-A records 0 filed months, and including 2018-2021 when Return-A recorded 7/10/9/6. A field that reads 12 unconditionally says nothing about 2024 exposure specifically. Against that, the agency has demonstrated both capacity and a real level -- four consecutive 12-month years at 10, 7, 14, 9, i.e. 1,085 per 100k, 2.15x the 503.4 peer median for its band -- and 2024 is an exactly uniform zero across all seven streams including the larceny (~5.8/yr) and MVT (~2.5/yr) workhorses. On a ~10/yr base a single zero year is ~4.5e-05 and two consecutive zeros ~2e-09, so composition and level together say the reporting relationship failed, not that crime ceased in a 922-person city: Return-A exposure erodes 7 -> 10 -> 9 -> 6 -> 2 -> 0 -> 0 in lockstep with the published totals. Since the total is 0, uplift cannot rescue it and token_reporting_flag would settle nothing -- no number of believable months returns anything but 0 -- so the year must go missing and be filled.

detail: 2024 must not stand as an observed measured full year. Set the agency-year MISSING and fillable. COMPOSITION: 2024 is uniformly zero across all seven streams, so it carries no internal signal either way - the work is done by provenance. OWN-HISTORY LAUNDERING avoided: the pipeline's 0.5 median is built out of five 0-filed-month years; the only honest anchor is 2022. ABSOLUTE PLAUSIBILITY does not by itself reject a zero at pop 889 (own demonstrated level ~1/yr, P(0)~37%) - the case turns on the record, not the value. ORI SUCCESSION: roster 2024 lists the agency live with nibrs_start 2025-07-01 and no NIBRS row in any year, i.e. an agency stranded between lanes, not a dead ORI, so no supersession and the footprint (place 3602143, w=1 exclusive) depends on this ORI being filled.

detail: MISSING + fill ≈4 (range 1-5). Anchors: the only 12-filed-month year on record (2019) is 1; the SPUB series 2021-23 is 4/6/1 (median 4); exposure-weighted FBI rate is 13 offences / 30 filed months = 0.43/month → 5.2/yr. rationale: The state lane cannot be read as a full-year zero for this particular agency, because its published totals reproduce the FBI partial sums exactly — SPUB 6 = the 5-month SRS 6 in 2022, SPUB 1 = the 3-month SRS 1 in 2023 — i.e. DCJS is publishing the sum of whatever months the agency filed, and in 2024 the FBI lane says that is one month. A 12-month zero resting on one filed month is a token record published as complete, and because uplift is multiplicative it cannot be repaired as a partial year (0 × 12 = 0), so the only usable repair is missing-and-fillable.

detail: 2024 must go MISSING rather than stand as an observed measured zero -- but the repair is numerically almost a no-op, and the load-bearing half of this ruling is what the fill must NOT be. Record: one filed month (SRS 1mo, total 0) behind CIUS 0/12mo and SPUB 0/12mo, both 12-month labels being pipeline defaults.
